promise: Remove BC's consumer carbon tax if Ottawa lifts national requirement
summary: Legislation tabled March 31, 2025 dropped the consumer carbon tax rate to $0, effective April 1, 2025.

promise: Ban doctor's notes for short absences
summary: Bill 11 amended the Employment Standards Act so employers cannot require a sick note for the first two short-term absences per year. In force November 12, 2025.

promise: Deliver a middle-class income tax cut
summary: Finance Minister Brenda Bailey confirmed on Feb 13, 2025 the $1,000-per-household middle-class tax cut (rebate in year one) would not be included in the March 4 budget, citing the U.S. tariff threat.

promise: Building more homes for renters and buyers
summary: BC Builds has broken ground on 4,000 units and over 99,000 homes are delivered or underway since 2017; B.C. asking rents are down 12.5% since Aug 2023.

promise: Fast-tracking BC's factory home construction
summary: The Digitally Accelerated Standardized Housing (DASH) program launched Nov 2025; first RFPs for prefab/modular demo projects (~90 homes in Prince George and Abbotsford) issued Feb 2026.

promise: Working with municipalities, private developers, non-profits and unions to drive home construction
summary: Local Government Development Approvals Program ($9M to 56 local governments via UBCM) and BC Builds are funding partnerships to speed approvals and construction.

promise: Open the door to more home ownership
summary: Attainable Housing Initiative with the MST Nations will deliver ~2,600 first homes at 40% below market at the Heather Lands (Province contributing up to $672M).

promise: Open up and protect homes for people
summary: Rental Protection Fund has safeguarded nearly 1,600 affordable rental homes since 2023; short-term rental restrictions returned thousands of units to long-term market.

promise: Provide safe, secure housing for everyone
summary: Federal Build Canada Homes partnership commits $170M federal plus up to $200M provincial to advance 700+ supportive and transitional homes.

promise: Strengthen protections for BC consumers
summary: Business Practices and Consumer Protection Act amendments (Feb 2025) ban high-pressure door-to-door sales and improve cancellation/subscription rules; second phase on credit-fraud tools Oct 2025.

promise: Freeze ICBC premiums
summary: ICBC basic rates are frozen with no increase through spring 2027 â€” seven consecutive years without a basic-rate increase.

promise: Offer free transit for seniors in non-peak hours
summary: No provincial announcement found introducing free transit for seniors during non-peak hours.

promise: Keep hydro rates low and support solar
summary: BC Hydro launched first-ever rooftop solar and battery-storage rebates (up to $5,000 each for homes) in July 2024; B.C. holds the second-lowest residential electricity rates in North America.

promise: Cut the cost of heating and cooling your home
summary: Expanded CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program (July 2024) offers up to $16,000 in heat-pump rebates (up to $24,000 in northern B.C.).

promise: Build more on- and off-reserve Indigenous housing
summary: BC Builds partnered with three First Nations to fast-track 235 on-reserve rental homes (construction started April 2025); ~6,800 Indigenous homes total since 2017.

promise: Create standardized online municipal building permit system
summary: The digital Building Permit Hub launched May 27, 2024, standardizing permit submissions with automated code checks across pilot jurisdictions.

promise: Bringing the certainty businesses are looking for
summary: B.C. launched an ease-of-doing-business review in June 2025 to streamline regulation and permitting.

promise: A sustainable future for forest workers, companies and communities
summary: Province announced the 'Make More in B.C.' project ($2M to FPInnovations) and legislative changes for BC Timber Sales to protect forestry jobs.

promise: Fast Track Priority Critical Mineral Projects
summary: B.C. became the first Canadian jurisdiction with fixed mineral-exploration permitting timelines (April 2026); first permits issued ahead of schedule.

promise: Build Out the Electricity Grid and Upgrade Northwest Highways for Mining
summary: Construction broke ground on the North Coast Transmission Line (Sept 2026) to power northwest mining/energy projects.

promise: Ensure Resource Development Benefits Communities and First Nations
summary: B.C. launched a First Nations Equity Financing Program and signed shared-prosperity and consent agreements with the Tahltan Nation and Simpcw First Nation.

promise: Deliver Food Security Through a Stronger Agricultural Industry
summary: B.C. continued Buy BC and farm-technology funding to strengthen food security, including labour-saving technology support for farmers in 2026.

promise: Help Protect Small Business Owners and Reduce Their Costs
summary: Province paused the PST expansion (~$260M saved) and raised the employer health tax exemption threshold.

promise: Cut Red Tape for Restaurants, Wineries, Breweries and Distilleries
summary: No post-election action found to cut red tape specifically for restaurants, wineries, breweries and distilleries.

promise: Strengthen Protections for BC Workers
summary: B.C. introduced job-protected medical leave (Employment Standards Act amendment), new crane-safety licensing, and improved the ESB complaint process.

promise: Partner for sustainable, innovative forestry
summary: B.C. announced the first candidate area for the Working Forest Landscape Model and continued value-added wood manufacturing and community-forest expansion.

promise: Double Apprenticeship Training
summary: A $241-million fund (Nov 2025) will double trades-training funding over three years and permanently expand apprenticeship seats.

promise: Making BC a clean energy superpower
summary: B.C. released its 'Powering Our Future' clean-energy strategy (June 2024) and advanced BC Hydro's first call for power in 15 years (nine wind projects, Dec 2024).

promise: Use government buying power to make clean energy technology more affordable
summary: New BC Hydro solar/battery rebates and expanded heat-pump rebates are lowering costs, though a distinct bulk-procurement program was not identified.

promise: Expand BC Hydro solar and battery rebates
summary: BC Hydro introduced first-ever rooftop solar and battery-storage rebates in mid-2024 (up to $10,000 for homes).

promise: Bulk purchase heat pumps to get better deals on energy retrofits
summary: Heat-pump rebates substantially expanded (~$50M April 2025 for up to 8,300 rebates, plus a condo/apartment program July 2025).

promise: Double public EV charging stations by 2030
summary: Public charging ports grew to 8,900+ by April 2026 (87% up from 2023); a $700M plan (July 2026) will add 3,500 more ports by 2035.

promise: Move BC's school bus fleet to electric
summary: First electric school buses entered service in Sooke School District (2021), but no provincewide electrification program found.

promise: Cap emissions from the oil and gas sector
summary: B.C. committed (March 2024) to a backstop to the federal oil-and-gas emissions cap, with provincial regulations planned; no confirmation of final regulation found.

promise: Expand the Youth Climate Corps
summary: Youth Climate Corps B.C. expanded to 11 communities; a further $1.4M announced June 2026.

promise: Phase out glyphosate use in BC forests
summary: No provincial action or announcement to phase out glyphosate in B.C. forests was found.

promise: Expand salmon restoration investment
summary: New joint B.C. Fisheries Fund (Aug 2026) and continued watershed/estuary restoration work.

promise: Made-in-BC biodiversity strategy
summary: B.C. released a draft Biodiversity and Ecosystem Health Framework (Nov 2023); no finalization found through 2026.

promise: Protect 30% of BC's lands and waters by 2030
summary: Three new conservation-planning projects (~127,000 ha) announced July 2026 explicitly support the 30x30 target.

promise: Complete Old Growth Strategic Review recommendations
summary: Implementation continuing (Fairy Creek old-growth deferral extended to Sept 2026; Working Forest Landscape Model advancing).

promise: Ramp up active forest management to protect communities from wildfire
summary: Budget 2026 includes new wildfire-prevention investments alongside ongoing FireSmart funding.

promise: Advance Sumas Prairie flood prevention
summary: $3.3M (Jan 2026) for the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative, building on ~$220M since 2021.

promise: Secure Clean Water for BC Communities
summary: Watershed security strategy being co-developed with First Nations and a $100M healthy-watershed investment announced; final strategy not yet released.

promise: Continue the Declaration Act Action Plan
summary: Annual Declaration Act implementation progress report published June 2026.

promise: Deliver regional land-use clarity with First Nations and communities
summary: Multiple regional land-use planning processes advancing with First Nations (Tahltan, Taku River Tlingit, Kaska Dena, Gitanyow, Nisga'a).

promise: Advance Indigenous education and language revitalization
summary: Supporting First Nations-led teacher-education programs with FNESC and IAHLA to increase First Nations K-12 teachers.

promise: Expand support for urban Indigenous people through Friendship Centres
summary: Pilot projects through Friendship Centres (Port Alberni, Kamloops, Prince George, Surrey, Nanaimo, Smithers) launched.

promise: Support people living with disabilities
summary: Continued disability supports including employment programs for blind/low-vision people, plus AccessibleBC standards work.

promise: Train, Hire and Keep More Health Professionals
summary: 765+ new nursing/allied-health seats, 40 more UBC med-school seats, SFU medical school opened (48 students, Aug 2026), 160+ new residency positions by 2028.

promise: Speed Up Licensing of Out-of-Province Health Care Providers
summary: New College of Physicians and Surgeons bylaws (July 6, 2026) allow internationally trained doctors from seven countries to apply directly for full licences; 1,200+ licensed in 2025.

promise: Address Regional Shortages of Health Care Professionals
summary: Internationally trained doctors/nurses being distributed across regions; shortages persist in rural/remote areas.

promise: Protecting you from the return of costly MSP premiums
summary: MSP premiums eliminated Jan 1, 2020 and remain eliminated with no reintroduction.

promise: Making sure everyone who wants a regular family doctor or nurse practitioner gets one
summary: ~4.47 million people (80%) have a primary care provider, but ~323,000 remain on the Health Connect Registry.

promise: More doctors, nurse practitioners and nurses
summary: Family doctors rose from 4,362 (2018) to 5,807 (2026); nurse practitioners tripled to 1,750+; 77,880 licensed nurses.

promise: Faster care with more choices
summary: Pharmacists can prescribe for 21 minor ailments and contraceptives since June 2023; more urgent/primary care centres opening.

promise: Building or expanding hospitals across BC
summary: Royal Columbian acute care tower (May 2026), Burnaby Hospital pavilion (March 2026), Surrey renal facility, and Royal Inland/Port Hardy upgrades.

promise: Better and faster cancer care through our 10-year plan
summary: 10-Year Cancer Action Plan ($440M, launched 2023) roughly three years in; 92 new cancer physicians and four regional cancer centres in development.

promise: End deadly cervical cancer within a decade
summary: First-in-Canada at-home HPV self-screening launched Jan 2024; free HPV vaccine program expanded July 2025.

promise: Increase job-protected leave for major medical diagnoses
summary: Employment Standards Act amendment created up to 27 weeks of job-protected leave for serious illness/injury, in effect Nov 28, 2025.

promise: Deliver faster access to cancer treatment
summary: 76.1% of patients receiving radiation within four weeks (up 11.1%); new regional cancer centres under construction.

promise: Improve cancer care through partnerships
summary: New BC Cancer centres being built with regional health authorities (Nanaimo construction Oct 2025; Kamloops underway).

promise: Make cancer care work better for you
summary: 10-Year Cancer Action Plan rolling out through new regional cancer centres and expanded HPV vaccine program.

promise: Streamline health care administration
summary: Health-authority review consolidating admin/corporate services into a shared-services organization (spring 2026); ~$60M+ annual savings expected.

promise: Let doctors treat patients
summary: New sick-note rules (Nov 2025) reduce paperwork; physician-assistant/scribe use is not yet provincewide.

promise: Deliver unified access to provincial health care resources
summary: Consolidating corporate/administrative services into one provincewide shared-services organization.

promise: Modernize and expand dignified disposition options
summary: First dedicated ash-dispersal site on a waterway (Fraser River, July 2026) and municipal guidelines published.

promise: Defend and expand access to reproductive health services
summary: First publicly funded IVF program (July 2025); midwives' scope expanded to prescribe Mifegymiso and contraceptives (2026).

promise: Create a comprehensive maternity care strategy
summary: New team-based Prince George Maternity Clinic (May 2026) and expanded midwifery scope.

promise: Fast-track cancer diagnosis and treatment
summary: ~93% of patients starting radiation within four weeks (Feb 2025), exceeding the 90% benchmark; BC Cancer ended its U.S. treatment program.

promise: Expand Foundry Centres for Youth
summary: Foundry Surrey Central opened Nov 2025; new Foundry centre in Terrace (May 2026).

promise: Single phone number for addiction treatment
summary: Access Central (single-point-of-entry addictions line) is live in Fraser, Interior, Island and Vancouver Coastal regions; Northern Health still to come.

promise: Expand access to high quality addiction treatment
summary: New withdrawal-management and First Nations-led treatment (Terrace, Haida Gwaii, Adams Lake); 3,700+ publicly funded addiction beds.

promise: Expand specialized treatment beds
summary: New 60-bed facility in Surrey underway; new complex-care beds opened at Alouette Homes (2025).

promise: Open secure care facilities under the Mental Health Act
summary: Mental Health Act amendments (Nov 2025); 132 involuntary-care beds in Surrey and Prince George; first beds opened at Alouette Homes (spring 2025).

promise: Expand nasal naloxone availability
summary: $50M investment expands nasal naloxone to ~half of 400,000+ kits, from 150 to all 2,400 take-home sites (April 2026).

promise: Designated mental health units in correctional centres
summary: Ten involuntary-care beds in a designated mental-health unit at Surrey Pretrial Services Centre.

promise: Security & Affordability For BC Seniors
summary: SAFER and Rental Assistance Program enhanced (April 2025) to help low-income seniors afford rent.

promise: More Nurses and Home Support for BC Seniors
summary: Expanded home-care supports (five-year Better at Home agreement) and streamlined credential recognition for U.S. nurses.

promise: Strengthen drug prevention education in schools
summary: PreVenture drug-prevention program expanded to 80+ schools in 20+ districts ($2M annual funding).

promise: Deliver affordable before- and after-school care
summary: Bill 19 (School Amendment Act, Oct 2025) lets school districts provide before/after-school child care and opt into fee reduction.

promise: Build new child care spaces
summary: ChildCareBC funded 41,500+ new licensed spaces (26,200+ open), with school-based spaces opening through 2026.

promise: Expand the school meals program
summary: Feeding Futures school food program continues delivering meals; no new post-election expansion announcement found.

promise: Getting You Where You Want To Go, Faster & Cleaner
summary: Expanded Metro Vancouver bus service (April 2025), new transit hours in Kelowna/Kamloops/Victoria (Jan 2026), Surrey Langley SkyTrain construction.

promise: Increase funding for amateur sports
summary: Continued Pathways to Sport funding ($400K/yr KidSport BC, $1.4M/yr Indigenous sport, $51M over 5 years for sport organizations).

promise: Create better camping experiences
summary: Campground improvements underway/completed (Rolley Lake added sites, Tribune Bay redesign, Paul Lake accessibility).

promise: Expand BC parks, recreation sites and trails
summary: Legislation (Feb 2025) expands three parks; 2026 Look West Outdoor Recreation Strategy and trail funding.

promise: Ramp up seizure of proceeds of organized crime
summary: Civil Forfeiture Act amendments (Feb 2026), expanded Civil Forfeiture Office, and claims against three Hells Angels clubhouses.

promise: Keep repeat violent and gang offenders off the streets
summary: Repeat Violent Offending Intervention Initiative expanded; federal bail/sentencing reforms received royal assent June 2026.

promise: Stop repeat offenders in their tracks
summary: Budget 2026 added $139M to reduce repeat offending; welcomed federal bail/sentencing reforms (June 2026).

promise: Make roads safer from reckless supercar drivers
summary: Dangerous-driving impound fees substantially increased (Aug 2024); no separate supercar-specific measure confirmed.

promise: Help women and families escape domestic abuse
summary: 229 transition/second-stage housing units (Mar 2025), 150+ more homes (Feb 2026), and further supports (Sept 2026).

promise: Strengthen Gender-Based Violence Action Plan
summary: $18M federal (Sept 2025) and $4.6M (April 2026) to deliver B.C.'s Gender-Based Violence Action Plan.

promise: Protect vulnerable groups with hate crime legislation
summary: Hate-crime offences are federal; B.C. welcomed proposed federal Criminal Code amendments (Sept 2025).

promise: Deliver health-focused crisis response to 911 calls
summary: Peer Assisted Care Teams expanded (Prince George, Comox Valley, Kamloops); further expansion announced June 2026.

promise: Support police to keep guns off our streets
summary: New Firearm Violence Prevention Act regulations (April 2026) and expanded Provincial Forensic Firearms Lab.

promise: Unify provincial enforcement teams into a single agency
summary: BC Compliance and Enforcement Agency (BC-CEA) established July 1, 2026, consolidating natural-resource enforcement.

promise: Keep public service ratios consistent with other provinces
summary: Budget 2026 commits to reduce the public sector by 15,000 FTEs over the fiscal plan.

promise: Keep debt-to-GDP among the lowest in Canada
summary: Net liabilities-to-GDP remains among the lowest, but taxpayer-supported debt-to-GDP projected to rise to 37.4% by 2028-29.

promise: Manage public finances sustainably while putting people first
summary: Budget 2025/2026 project declining deficits and $3.5B in expenditure-management savings while protecting core services.

promise: Eliminate the Electricity Surtax
summary: Passed 6-1 (Nov 6) — Voted 6-1 to eliminate the 3.5% climate action levy effective Jan 1, 2027; removes ~$2M/yr of climate funding with no stated replacement plan (Henderson's question unanswered). Fontaine's inaugural speech claimed eliminating the surtax will save ratepayers over $8 million over the term.

promise: Create a Financial Accountability and Budget Oversight Committee
summary: Passed unanimous (Nov 6) — Unanimously approved (Folka chair); Henderson criticized the structure for excluding most of council from budget decisions.

promise: Reduce External Consultant Spending
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 6-1 (2027 cut; future-years cut unanimous) (Nov 6 agenda item 2.7) — Staff directed to cut consultants 10% (2027) and plan for 20% over two years — a target and a plan, not a cut; no reduction has actually occurred.

promise: Eliminate Patio Permit Fees and Expand Patio Seating
summary: [100-Day Plan] Discussed (Nov 6 agenda item 4.7(b)) — Only the patio permit fee is addressed ('bring forward bylaw amendments'); the +25% seating expansion goal is absent, and nothing has been enacted yet.

promise: Cancel the 'Sue Big Oil' Initiative
summary: [100-Day Plan] Discussed (Nov 6 agenda item 2.8) — Staff directed to cancel the ~$90,000 spend, but 'subject to existing legal or contractual obligations' — cancellation not yet confirmed. West Coast Environmental Law wrote to council (Nov 6) opposing the withdrawal, warning taxpayers 'may be on the hook' for ever-increasing climate costs.

promise: Place at least 12 new Community Enforcement and Safety Officers
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 6-1 (Nov 6 agenda item 2.9) — Directed into the 2027 budget as an exception to the hiring freeze — no officers hired; staffing plan, costs and deployment timeline are still to come.

promise: Enhance street cleaning and add 100 new waste and recycling bins
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 6-1 (Nov 6 agenda item 4.3) — Staff directed to 'develop and begin' an accelerated program — a plan, not yet cleaner streets or any of the 100 bins installed.

promise: Establish a Crime Reduction and Public Safety Task Force
summary: Discussed (Nov 6 agenda item 6.2(1)) — Only 'approved in principle' as a Committee, with terms of reference due Jan 30, 2027 — it does not exist yet.

promise: Create a new Amateur Sport and Recreation Council
summary: Discussed (Nov 6 agenda item 6.2(5)) — Only 'approved in principle', with terms of reference due Jan 30, 2027 — the council is not yet functioning.

promise: Fix New Westminster's worst traffic bottlenecks
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 7-0 (Nov 6 agenda item 4.8) — Staff directed to 'identify' the 20 worst bottlenecks — identification, not fixes; no improvements delivered.

promise: Bring Political Leadership Back to Rail Issues
summary: [100-Day Plan] Discussed (Nov 6 agenda item 6.2(4)) — Railway Community Advisory Panel 'approved in principle' — not yet convened, no meetings held.

promise: Advocate to reduce train whistles
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 7-0 (Nov 6 agenda item 4.9) — Staff directed to re-establish the RCAP and 'develop an updated action plan' — planning only; no whistle-cessation outcome or new quiet zone advanced.

promise: Create the Columbia District
summary: Passed 7-0 (Nov 6) — Voted 7-0 to create the Mayor's Task Force on Economic Development & Columbia District Revitalization; micro-retail still only 'identified', nothing built. Fontaine's inaugural speech pledged at least 10 micro-retail spaces within 24 months.

promise: Freeze mayor, council and senior executive pay
summary: [100-Day Plan] Discussed (Nov 6 agenda item 2.2) — Freeze directed 'subject to applicable legislative and contractual obligations' — a motion, not an enacted freeze. Fontaine estimated the pay freeze saves ~$600,000 next year.

promise: Launch an independent core services review
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 6-1 (Nov 6 agenda item 4.2 and 5) — Terms of reference still to be developed and the three-person panel not yet struck — the review has not started.
evidence_source: 2026-11-06 Special Council Meeting — agenda item 4.2 and 5

promise: Give residents their voice back
summary: Passed 6-1 (Nov 6) — Community Advisory Assembly dissolved 6-1; 7 select committees approved; Henderson's motion to defer until the strategic plan was defeated.

promise: Make New West the Royal City again
summary: Passed 6-1 (Nov 6) — Voted 6-1 to halt the rebrand and restore the crown logo; Henderson's amendment to consult Host Nations first was defeated 6-1.

promise: Get the waterfront pier rebuild moving
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 7-0 as amended (Nov 6 agenda item 4.4) — Only a 'report within 6 months' is promised — no plan, cost estimate, or timeline delivered yet.

promise: Strengthen City–School District Collaboration
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 7-0 (Nov 6 agenda item 4.5) — Staff directed to 'review and strengthen' coordination — no new joint structure or agreement is in place.

promise: Publish Council agendas at least 7 calendar days before meetings
summary: Already broken: the new council's first substantive meeting (Special Council, Fri Nov 6, 1:00pm) had its agenda package timestamped Nov 5 — roughly one day's notice, not the promised 7 calendar days. The platform's 'whenever possible' caveat does not excuse their own inaugural act falling short of their transparency pledge.

promise: Eliminate the automatic transportation allowance for elected officials
summary: Passed unanimously (Nov 6 agenda item 2.3) — Council directed staff to eliminate the automatic transportation allowance and replace it with a reimbursement model, but capped 'at an annual maximum equivalent to the current allowance' — a re-label that may yield little or no actual saving.

promise: Restore Council's final approval authority for City grants
summary: Discussed (Nov 6 agenda item 8) — Motion rescinds the CAO's delegation to approve community grants and requires all grant recommendations to come before Council — direction only; no grant decisions have changed hands yet.

promise: Keep citizen delegations at every regular Council meeting
summary: No action in the first meeting. The commitment is to preserve and expand a standing public-input right; nothing has yet been delivered or codified.

promise: Hold Council debate and discussion in public
summary: No action in the first meeting; a critical gap given the new council's own transparency framing.

promise: Release in-camera reports once confidentiality ends
summary: No action or policy in the first meeting.

promise: Restore staff liaisons for residents' associations
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Meet with residents' associations twice a year
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Allow residents' associations to submit resolutions to Council
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Improve communication on major City projects
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Review the Be Heard engagement system within 100 days
summary: The 100-day clock is running from Nov 6; no independent review has been announced or commissioned.

promise: Modernize the Council Procedure Bylaw
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Remove limits on councillor motions
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Establish a Youth Council
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Make committee appointments reflect expertise and diversity
summary: No action in the first meeting; the two public members of the Finance Committee were still 'to be appointed'.

promise: Increase voter turnout by 5% by 2030
summary: No action in the first meeting. Fontaine noted turnout already rose to 40% (from 27%); the +5% target is on top of that.

promise: Establish twice-yearly New Westminster Caucus meetings
summary: No caucus schedule published; no action in the first meeting. Fontaine said he will chair the inaugural New West Caucus early next year.

promise: Develop a First Nations and Indigenous engagement framework
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Publish a report on senior government downloading
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: Build stronger crisis response capability within 100 days
summary: The 100-day clock is running from Nov 6; no plan has been announced.

promise: Mayor to represent the City on Metro Vancouver without extra pay
summary: No action in the first meeting.

promise: End partisan appointments and balance them among all councillors
summary: The first meeting spread committee chairs across all six councillors — including Community First councillor Tasha Henderson, who chairs Planning, Housing and Public Engagement — but the two public members on the Finance Committee remain unfilled, so the non-partisan/balanced-appointment pledge is only partially evidenced.

promise: Modernize City Hall
summary: [100-Day Plan] Passed 6-1 (Nov 6 agenda item 4.6) — Staff directed to develop terms of reference for a Red Tape Reduction Task Force and a Permit Concierge; no faster approvals or red-tape reduction delivered yet.

promise: Rebrand 'Downtown New Westminster' to the new Columbia District
summary: Passed 7-0 (Nov 6) — Voted 7-0 to create the Mayor's Task Force on Economic Development & Columbia District Revitalization; Henderson opposed the 'Columbia' name over its colonial origins (Royal Engineers displaced Indigenous villages).

promise: Traffic flow: new Queensborough Bridge or third crossing
summary: Fontaine's inaugural speech made a new Queensborough Bridge a signature priority — he will ask council to back talks with the province on a replacement or another crossing. No action yet.

promise: Keep SkyTrain stations clean and secure
summary: Fontaine's inaugural speech pledged to work with TransLink to improve New Westminster and Columbia stations. No action yet.
